lead: Aerospace & Defense ETF / ITA — the war trade gets its Reddit moment
smaller: 3x Nasdaq 100 ETF / TQQQ — the invasion dip, bought the same day
Tesla / TSLA — the SEC turns to Musk's own selling
Coinbase Global / COIN — the crypto broker warns its crowd is cooling
why_lead: The war trade on the first day of the invasion (n1262), with the month's clearest named retail-attention evidence: Fortune reports Reddit's WallStreetBets celebrating war-friendly stocks as the Nasdaq and S&P rebounded (n0748), plus Masterworks' defence-contractor guide (n0781). The 2022-02-23 retail edition (Brent, DWAC, SoFi, AMC) declined a defence carryover for lack of new evidence; this edition has it. Own-card move (2022-02-24 sessions): ITA +2.75% to 104.49 USD, NOC +2.44%, RTX +2.18%, LMT +1.75% to 395.71 USD, Rheinmetall +3.38% to 100.05 EUR against DAX -3.96%, STOXX 600 -3.28%, FTSE 100 -3.88%; S&P 500 +1.50%, Nasdaq 100 +3.44%, Brent 99.08 USD +2.31%. Catalysts: Reuters on European defence stocks rising (n0690), BAE's sharper-focus comment (n0665), US and UK sanctions (n1281, n1286), White House 'all options' (n0227). Analog/break: the Russian leg of the same pre-war flow trade (FT n0843) crashed 33% (n0763, n0761), Bloomberg's fifth-worst-in-history ranking (n0762). Smart money hedged with gold and bonds instead (n0800, n1164, n1644). Chronology: material update and promotion of the 2022-02-24 secondary item 'Aerospace & Defense ETF / ITA — buying the arsenal and the target'. That item was pre-invasion, based only on the FT flow report and a defence leg that had barely moved (ITA -1.14%); this lead rests entirely on newly published 24 February evidence (the invasion, WallStreetBets coverage, European defence rally, BAE, the Russian crash that broke the other leg) and a materially different reaction (ITA +2.75%). Defence first appeared as the 2022-02-22 secondary item 'Lockheed Martin / LMT — the war trade finally gets its trigger', when the trade had not yet worked (LMT -2.46% over five sessions); no earlier retail edition (2022-02-01, -02, -03, -07, -08, -09, -14, -15, -21, -22, -24 available) led with defence, and none of the 22 or 24 February defence evidence is re-cited except the FT flow report as the setup for the Russian leg.
why_smaller: 3x Nasdaq 100 ETF / TQQQ: brief carryover (156 words, under the 160-word cap) of the 2022-02-24 lead (itself a promotion of a 2022-02-22 secondary item), kept secondary because the narrative is unchanged but the outcome is new: TQQQ +9.79% to 49.56 USD, Nasdaq 100 +3.44%, ARKK +7.79%, AMC +12.40%, Opendoor +19.09%, Upstart +17.01% (prior close 2022-02-24), with the BBC's shares-rebound headline (n0742); breaks on TQQQ still -13.49% over five sessions and VIX 30.32.

Tesla / TSLA: material update of the 2022-02-21 smaller item 'Tesla / TSLA — Musk picks a fight with the SEC' (Musk's harassment complaints and the braking probe). The new catalyst, published 24 February, reverses the direction of the regulator story: WSJ reports the SEC probing trading by Musk and his brother after the CEO's share sales (n0694), with the Guardian's insider-trading framing (n0687); bull counter from Reuters' Shanghai capacity report (n1760) and Musk's $140B wealth loss (n1643). Card TSLA +4.81% to 800.77 USD on the Nasdaq rebound but -13.28% 5-session, -14.58% 20-session from 937.41 USD. None of the 21 February evidence is re-cited and the hook was changed to the new probe.

Coinbase Global / COIN: a distinct retail-activity census narrative from newly released results: revenue beat (n0679) but a caution on, and expected fall in, first-quarter trading volume (n0678, n0679), with bitcoin's safe-haven claims questioned (n0860); COIN 179.56 USD +3.95% in the regular session, -13.66% 5-session; BTC 38,332.61 USD +2.78% (prior completed daily close 2022-02-24), -7.63% over 20 observations. 2022-02-15 used Coinbase for the Super Bowl QR-ad app crash; the catalyst and narrative here are new (results and volume guidance). The bitcoin haven-failure angle used on 2022-02-18 and 2022-02-21 appears only as one supporting line with a new 24 February headline (n0860).
considered_not_chosen: Gold / GC=F and GLD (Reuters gold ETF inflows n1164, Yahoo Finance UK one-year high n0706, Mining.com 15-month peak n1761, CNBC 'resist the rush' n1644; GC=F 1,926.30 USD/oz +0.83% but GLD -0.65% and GDX -1.93%): folded into the lead's Smart Money View as the professional hedge; gold ran as a retail item on 2022-02-14 and 2022-02-21 and a separate item would recycle the haven story.

Cybersecurity (PANW +13.05% to 539.94 USD, CRWD +13.01%, ZS +10.02%, NET +18.66% with Cloudflare's Area 1 deal n0677): large moves but only indirect headline support (n0662 cyber-risk framing), and the moves coincided with the broad Nasdaq rebound already carried by the TQQQ item.
Moderna / MRNA (+15.10% on a fourth-quarter beat and 2022 vaccine-sales outlook, n0727, n0729, n0730): strong results story but no crowd-attention evidence.
Wheat / ZW=F (926.00 US cents/bu, +5.71%, +18.64% 5-session; Reuters grains spike n1774): unchanged continuation of the 2022-02-24 item; not repeated.
Polish and Austrian banks and LPP (LPP -25.19%, RBI -23.14%, PKO -16.82%) and SocGen (-12.15%): Russia-exposure crashes, institutional rather than retail stories.
Digital World Acquisition / DWAC (87.32 USD, -1.33%): no material update since 2022-02-24.
Block / SQ results: no eligible outcome headline; ABC's 'ASX rebounds... Block soars' (n0074) avoided as describing the 25 February ASX session after the cutoff.

Avoided as possibly after the cutoff or live/rolling pages: n0074 (25 February ASX session), n0717 (Reuters LIVE MARKETS blog), n0128 (Reuters 'Expert views' rolling compilation); no EU-summit second-package outcome used.
